patch_description:
This crossover-driven proposal integrates the best-performing elements from the two reference implementations:
- Symmetry-aware, per-group pre- and post- RZ gates (corners/edges/center) to exploit Tic-Tac-Toe geometry.
- Independent, group-shared RY rotations (corners/edges/center) for expressive yet parameter-efficient encoding.
- Ring entanglement on the outer border using CRX with a single shared parameter to promote coherent perimeter correlations.
- Hub entanglement between the center and edges using CRY with per-edge unique parameters to increase flexibility without exploding parameter count.
- Post-entanglement RZ rotations still shared per group.

This design aims to improve validation/test performance by increasing expressivity where it matters (ring and hub interactions) while keeping parameter count manageable through targeted sharing. The rest of the training loop, data construction, feature map, and measurements remain unchanged to ensure fair comparisons. The approach preserves the same inputs/outputs and hardware-constrained connectivity, while potentially narrowing the train/test gap observed in prior runs.
